project.title: wipEU
project.description: Analyzing women's representation in the EU.
project.introText: wipEU is an open data project on how the representation of women in positions of power and decision-making correlates across the European Union, and how it has changed over time.

gridImages.caption: Replaying EU agency boards from 2003, mid-transition, in dark mode.
Pace to parity: a straight-line trend through the last ten years puts parity between 2031 (research boards) and 2071 (Court of Justice), stated as a projection.
Map and ranked list by country, with a year slider and role picker; the view is kept in the URL.
Country profiles: Italy compared with France and the EU-27 across three datasets, with a shareable link.

project.middleText: We combined EIGE datasets across six areas (public administration, business and finance, politics, environment and climate change, education and research, law and institutions) into new mashup datasets, and assessed their quality, legal and ethical aspects as open data. In 2023, for example, women made up 20% of the highest decision-making bodies of European financial institutions and led 26.8% of major political parties. In 2026 I redesigned the site around seats: a hemicycle for each body with one dot per real person and a year playback, a pace-to-parity projection, a country map and profiles you can compare and share, and a light/dark switch, set in Newsreader and Public Sans.
project.conclusionText: Final project for Open Access and Digital Ethics (2023/24, University of Bologna) with Salvatore Di Marzo and Matteo Guenci. I worked on the idea, data retrieval, the visualisations, the quality and legal analyses and the website, built with Leaflet and Plotly.js. The mashup datasets are released under CC BY 4.0.
project.highlightCaption: The chamber: one dot per person. In 2023, 44 of the 164 leaders of major political parties in the EU-27 were women.
project.context: Open Access and Digital Ethics, 2023/24, MA Digital Humanities and Digital Knowledge, University of Bologna
project.reworkNote: wipEU began as a group project with Salvatore Di Marzo and Matteo Guenci for Open Access and Digital Ethics (2023/24). I reworked it independently in 2026; the version shown here is that rework.
